title: Microbatch pad-peeling with prefill hints and kernel affinity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce wasted compute and tokens from padding by introducing a prefill-aware microbatch shaping algorithm we call 'pad-peeling'. This feature combines a lightweight per-request prefill hint, runtime sequence-length clustering, and kernel-affinity annotations so the scheduler can produce microbatches that minimize padding while honoring latency SLOs.
background: Current continuous-batching causes high pad overhead when request seq lengths have a long tail. Existing length bucketing reduces waste but is static and often misaligns with prefill vs decode phases. We want a runtime-aware approach that: 1) uses a short prefill probe to classify requests, 2) peels long-tail tokens into separate microbatches, and 3) surfaces kernel affinity so the kernel selector can pick the best execution path for each shaped microbatch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end integration passes CI and can be toggled via runtime flag. 2) In production-like load tests, pad token volume reduces by >=15% on mixed workloads compared to baseline bucketing. 3) Average token cost reduction >=10% with p95 latency change <=5% and p99 latency impact <=10%. 4) No regression on correctness/outputs vs control for 5 canonical prompt sets. 5) Feature has tech docs and a Console dashboard tile showing pad savings.
design_decisions: Use single-query prefill hint: runtime samples first N tokens (configurable, default N=8) to estimate seqlen cohort and attention mode.
Pad-peeling: allow long requests to be split into a small prefill microbatch and a separate tail microbatch to avoid dragging short requests into large-pad batches.
Kernel affinity tags: microbatch objects carry lightweight hints (e.g., dense-kernel, sparse-attention, kv-prefill) to guide kernel selection without hard binding.
Latency-first policy: when latency SLOs are tight, prefer smaller microbatches with slightly higher pad to maintain p95; cost-first policy active under lower latency constraints.
Graceful fallback: if affinity mismatch or kernel unavailable, fall back to existing bucketing to preserve correctness.
Telemetry: emit per-route pad bytes, microbatch size distribution, kernel-choice breakdown and cost delta for offline analysis.
Safety: no user-visible change to output ordering or tokens; all splitting happens at runtime and is transparent to clients.

experiments: benchmarks: local-latency-suite/large-models (run artifacts in CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/5492)
implementation_notes: Add 'prefill_hint' field to incoming request envelope (optional, runtime-populated for auto-probe).
Scheduler changes: new microbatch shaping step between request queue and kernel assignment.
Kernel selector reads affinity tags and tries soft-matching to preferred kernels; implement scoring function that considers seqlen, mem footprint, and estimated throughput.
Ensure KV-cache semantics preserved when splitting: tail microbatch must remap to same conversation KV namespace and preserve offsets.
Metrics: add pad_token_count, pad_token_ratio, shaped_microbatch_ratio, kernel_affinity_hit.
risks: Incorrect splitting could increase latency for p99 if scheduling misorders tails; mitigation: strict ordering invariants and latency-first policy.
Kernel affinity mismatch may cause extra kernel-switching overhead; mitigation: soft hints and thresholded affinity acceptance.
Telemetry gaps if users disable prefill probe; mitigation: support client-supplied hints and conservative defaults.
Complexity in rollback during incidents; mitigation: feature flag and per-route gating.
tests: Unit: prefill probe estimator with synthetic seq length distributions
Integration: end-to-end staging run with KV cache continuity checks
Performance: 48-hour soak with mixed ratio chat:completion 70:30; compare pad tokens and cost metrics
Fuzz: random split points to validate correctness and ordering
rollout_plan: Gate behind runtime flag 'pad_peeling' with per-route override
Start with internal-only traffic for 72 hours, collect pad and latency metrics
Enable for 10% of low-priority public traffic; monitor cost and latency dashboards
Gradually increase to 50% if pad savings and latency thresholds hold; provide rollback button in Console
Full rollout only after release window and ops playbook updated
